section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: The First Derivative
section_1.content: Briefly recap that the first derivative f'(x) represents the instantaneous rate of change (slope of the tangent line). Visually demonstrate a curve where f'(x) shows velocity.
section_1.example: A cheetah running: f(t) is position, f'(t) is velocity (how fast position changes over time).

section_2.title: Defining the Second Derivative
section_2.content: Introduce the second derivative f''(x) as the derivative of the first derivative. Explain it as the 'rate of change of the rate of change.' Use an animation showing how the slope of the tangent line itself increases or decreases.
section_2.example: The cheetah begins to accelerate; f''(t) represents acceleration (how velocity changes over time).

section_3.title: Higher Orders (n-th derivatives)
section_3.content: Generalize the concept to n-th derivatives (f''', f^(4), etc.). Explain that while higher orders are less intuitive, they measure the 'jerk' (rate of change of acceleration) or the curvature of a path.
section_3.example: A rocket launch: 1st derivative is velocity, 2nd is acceleration, 3rd is 'jerk' (the sudden change in force felt by astronauts).

section_4.title: Visualizing Curvature
section_4.content: Connect f''(x) to the geometry of the function. Show a concave-up graph (f''(x) > 0) vs. a concave-down graph (f''(x) < 0). Use a bouncing ball animation to show the direction of force.
section_4.example: A ball bouncing on a trampoline: the shape of the path is determined by the negative second derivative at the peak of the bounce.

section_5.title: Summary & Synthesis
section_5.content: Conclude with a 'Derivative Hierarchy' table. Emphasize that higher-order derivatives provide a deeper 'DNA' of the motion or curve, allowing us to predict future behavior beyond simple speed.
section_5.example: Applying this to stock market trend analysis or self-driving car braking systems, where smooth deceleration depends on controlling the 3rd derivative.

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.0 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
